newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, seen drifting.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index closed 0.68 percent lower on Thursday following selling pressure before the ascension day holiday and traders said the market was likely to drift over the next week.

"Many brokers feel better if they sell some of their shares before leaving on holiday. Most of the volume is usually accounted for by foreigners and they do not sell, so there was not much profit-taking," said Zoran Spasenic, a trader at brokerage BPH.
The SBI index eased 0.68 percent or 11.02 points to 1,600.40. This week the index has risen 1.49 percent.

"Most people here think that our market grows rapidly, when it is growing about 10 percent over the short term. But if you compare it to other emerging markets which have risen really fast recently, there is still a lot of room for rises," one trader said.
"When there is more foreign competition in September or October prices will rise much faster. By then the index could reach 1,800 points," Spasenic said.
Overall eight shares rose, nine fell and three were flat while seven were untraded. Turnover fell to 167.8 million tolars from 280.3 million.
Drug maker Lek was the most actively traded stock, easing 0.30 percent to 36,690 tolars on volume of 2,421 shares.
Preferred shares of trading firm Kovinotehna led the decliners, tumbling 4.12 percent to 512 tolars on volume of 135 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the top gainer, jumping 9.76 percent to 8,660 tolars on volume of 297 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
